full_judgment: 2. The short facts, the disposal of the this appeal and civil petition are that the respondent Nos.1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid suit for declaration of their title alleging that the land respondent No.1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid suit for declaration of their title alleging that the land appertaining to C.S. and S.A. Khatian Nos.23 and 23/2 and plot Nos. 544, 545, 546, 551, 552, 553, 554, 555, 556, 5560, 561, 562, 563, 564, 565, 567, 568, 569, 597, 598 and 599 measuring an area originally belonged to Abdul Samad Munshi, Abdul Jabbar Munshi, Moulavi Abdul Hakim and Kulsum Bibi to the extent of 4 annas shares each under the landlord Ramnarayan Roy Chowdhury and others. By amicable arrangement, Abdul Jabbar Munshi got the land of C.S. Khatian No.23/2, and S.A. Khatian No.9 and plot No.557 measuring an area of 33 acre in his share. He died leaving two sons namely, Md. Shamsuddin and Md. Abdul Gani. The lands of the plots, mentioned above, were acquired in L.A. Case Nos.138/1961-62 but the owners did not get any compensation. The plaintiffs, that is the heirs of Abdul Jabbar Munshi have been Possessing the said land of plot No.557 and in S.A. operation the same was duly recorded I their names. They have dwelling homestead in the said land. On 04.06.2011 the plaintiffs went to pay rent of the suit land to the Government but the defendant No. 4, denied to accept the same claiming that the suit land is the acquitted land of the Government. Knowing about it, the plaintiffs prayed to the authority concerned to get release of the property but in vain. Hence was the suit.
